title: The Lesson I Learned From Joseph’s Coat Being Stripped
paragraphs:
The Lesson I Learned From Joseph’s Coat Being Stripped
(Genesis 37:23)
They took his coat.
Not his calling.
Genesis 37:23 says Joseph’s brothers “stripped Joseph of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him.”
Read that again.

They could remove what marked him.
They could mock what favored him.
They could throw him into a pit.
But they could not cancel what God had spoken.
Some of you know exactly what that feels like.

You were stripped of trust.
Stripped of dignity.
Stripped of family support.
Stripped of the version of life you thought you would have.
And the enemy whispered, “Now you are nothing.”
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
A stripped coat is not a stripped destiny.
Joseph lost the garment, but not the God who gave the dream.
God saw it.
You knew the betrayal hurt deeper because it came from people close enough to recognize your coat.

But Genesis 50:20 gives the reveal:
“You meant evil against me; but God meant it for good.”
That is the Gospel pattern.
Jesus was also stripped.
“They stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe.” (Matthew 27:28)
The innocent Son of God was shamed publicly, nailed brutally, and crushed for sinners like us.
Not because we were good.
Because we were guilty.

Sin stripped us of righteousness.
Pride stripped us of truth.
Rebellion stripped us of life with God.
But Jesus took the shame so grace could cover us.
“By grace are ye saved through faith… not of works.” (Ephesians 2:8–9)
So repent.

Stop clinging to the coat they took.
Come to Christ, who gives a robe no enemy can remove.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
